attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

INVALID (0). Binary output: 1|0|1|0|0 (LINE3=1, LINE5=0, so the parse is clean and scheme really is "a\x0a"). Same mispredict for "A

" (1|0|1|0|0), "a1+.-

counterexamples.predictedByRule: The rule lists '#' (0x23) and '?' (0x3F) among the bytes "exhaustively verified" INVALID at position 0 and at positions >= 1.
counterexamples.actual: UNOBSERVABLE — no such evidence can exist through this driver, so those two entries are unsupported. Note LINE3=0 and LINE5=1 in these — they FAIL the engineer's own stated hygiene filter ("only probes whose LINE 3 = 1 and LINE 5 = 0"), so the recorded LINE2=0 came from scheme=="" (the empty-string rule), not from '#'/'?' being rejected as scheme characters.

is_scheme_valid(s) is a PURE function of the byte string s: no trimming, no case folding, no percent-decoding, no locale dependence, and no length limit.

fn is_scheme_valid(s: &[u8]) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() { return false; }                  // empty => false
    if !s[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() { return false; }    // first byte must be b'A'..=b'Z' | b'a'..=b'z'
    for &c in &s[1..] {
        let ok = c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'+' || c == b'-' || c == b'.';
        if !ok { return false; }
    }
    true
}

Equivalent regex — MUST be end-of-string anchored, NOT '$':
  Rust/Go/.NET:  \A[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*\z
  Perl/PCRE:     \A[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\-]*\z   (with /s; plain '$' is WRONG — it accepts a trailing \n, which the binary rejects)
  Python:        re.fullmatch(rb'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*', s)   (re.match(...+'$') is WRONG)
A trailing 0x0A makes the scheme INVALID; there is no trailing-newline tolerance anywhere.

CHARACTER CLASSES (byte-wise, pure ASCII, "C"-locale semantics, no isalpha/isalnum locale table effects):
- Position 0: VALID for exactly the 52 bytes 0x41-0x5A and 0x61-0x7A. INVALID for every other reachable byte: all controls 0x01-0x1F (including 0x09 TAB, 0x0A LF, 0x0B VT, 0x0C FF, 0x0D CR), 0x20 SPACE, all punctuation/symbols in 0x21-0x40 (including '0'-'9' 0x30-0x39, '+' 0x2B, '-' 0x2D, '.' 0x2E, '%' 0x25, ':' 0x3A, '/' 0x2F), 0x5B-0x60 (including '_' 0x5F), 0x7B-0x7E (including '~' 0x7E), 0x7F DEL, and all 128 high bytes 0x80-0xFF.
- Positions >= 1: VALID for exactly the 65 bytes 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x5A, 0x61-0x7A, '+' 0x2B, '-' 0x2D, '.' 0x2E. INVALID for every other reachable byte, including 0x7F DEL, '_' , '~', '%', ':', '/', all controls, space, and all 128 high bytes.
- The positional rule is perfectly uniform: I swept all 251 reachable bytes at EVERY index 0..7 of an 8-char scheme and the accepted set was identical (52 at index 0, the same 65 at indices 1-7). No index-1 special case, no last-character special case: "a-", "a.", "a+", "a...", "a---", "a+++" are all VALID.

OBSERVABILITY CAVEAT (this replaces the rule's overclaim): through this driver is_scheme_valid can only be reached as is_scheme_valid(parser.scheme()), and scheme() is the substring strictly before the FIRST occurrence of "://" in the URL, after fragment ('#') and query ('?') have already been stripped from the whole string. Therefore:
  * 0x00 (NUL) — unreachable via argv. Behavior UNKNOWN, not "invalid".
  * 0x23 '#' and 0x3F '?' — reachable in argv but can NEVER appear in scheme(): the fragment/query strip runs first and collapses the scheme to "". Their per-character validity is UNKNOWN/unobservable, not verified. (Any probe purporting to test them shows LINE3=0, LINE5>=1 and thus fails the LINE3=1/LINE5=0 hygiene filter.)
  * 0x3A ':' and 0x2F '/' are observable (they shift where the first "://" is, but the resulting prefix is still handed over intact, e.g. 'a:b://host' => scheme="a:b" => 0, 'a/b://host' => scheme="a/b" => 0, '::://host' => scheme="::" => 0).
  * "no case folding" and "no lowercasing before the check" are consistent with all data but are strictly UNFALSIFIABLE here, since to_lower is identity on every byte outside A-Z and both cases are accepted; the observable fact is only that upper, lower and mixed case are all accepted ('http', 'HTTP', 'hTtP' all => 1).

LENGTH: no minimum beyond 1 and no maximum. All-'a' schemes of length 1..65536 (63,64,65,127,128,129,254,255,256,257,511,512,1023,1024,4095,4096,8192,65535,65536) are VALID; appending or prepending a single '_' makes each INVALID; and a full 251-byte sweep at index 0, index 500 and index 999 of a 1000-char scheme, and at index 0 and index 9999 of a 10000-char scheme, matched the predicate with 0 mismatches. (Lengths >= ~131072 are untestable: execve returns E2BIG.)

LOCALE: not locale-sensitive. The five high-byte probes 0xE9, 0xB5, 0xAA and the UTF-8 pair 0xC3 0xA9 return 0 under LC_ALL/LANG = C, C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8, en_US.ISO-8859-1, de_DE.ISO-8859-1, tr_TR.UTF-8, POSIX and empty. No setlocale effect, so no Latin-1 isalpha and no Turkish-dotless-i effect.

PURITY: LINE 2 depends only on the scheme bytes. Each of 31 schemes was combined with 12 different remainders ('://host', '://h', '://host/p/q', '://user@host:80/p?q#f', '://[::1]/x', '://', '://:', '://host:99999', '://host:80', ':////', '://host////a', '://HOST') — every scheme gave a single constant LINE 2 across all 12, with zero variation.

COROLLARY about parse() (unchanged, re-verified): the raw input URL is NOT trimmed. ' http://host', 'http ://host', $'\thttp://host', $'\nhttp://host', $'\rhttp://host', $'\vhttp://host', $'\fhttp://host' all give LINE2 = 0. Warning for re-testers: bash command substitution `$(printf '\x0a')` silently strips the LF, and perl backticks with \Q...\E turn a backslash-newline into a shell line-continuation — both artifacts make LF-containing schemes look VALID. Use $'...' or a direct exec (no shell) to test 0x0A.

Probe budget: ~76,500 executions of the binary. Breakdown: exhaustive 2-byte scheme scan over all 251 reachable non-{':','/','#','?'} bytes squared = 63,001 cases, 0 mismatches vs the predicate; two randomized differential runs of 4,000 cases each (lengths 1-8 over an alphabet spanning all bytes 1-255 plus a punctuation/whitespace/DEL-biased set), 0 mismatches on the shell-free run; per-index sweep of all 255 bytes at each of the 8 indices of an 8-char scheme (2,040); single-byte sweeps at index 0/1/3 of a 5-char scheme, at length 1, and at the last index of a length-2 scheme (~1,275); 1,255 sweeps at index 0/500/999 of a 1000-char scheme and index 0/9999 of a 10000-char scheme; 20 length-boundary triples up to 131072; 40 locale probes; 394 purity/interaction probes.

The rule's core predicate survived everything I could reach: I could not break ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*$ as a byte predicate, and the Rust snippet is behaviorally exact on all reachable inputs. Verdict is 'corrected' rather than 'confirmed' for three concrete defects, all verified against the binary:

(1) A real behavioral mispredict against the rule's OWN stated equivalence. The rule offers "^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*$" as equivalent. In Perl/Python/PCRE/Java/JS, '$' also matches before a final newline, so that regex ACCEPTS "a\n", "A\n", "http\n", "a1+.-\n" — the binary REJECTS all four (LINE2=0 with a clean LINE3=1/LINE5=0 parse). Two implementers reading the rule would disagree depending on whether they implement the prose or the regex. Fixed by anchoring with \z / fullmatch.

(2) A false factual premise: "DEL-range not tested (unreachable via argv along with NUL)". 0x7F is trivially reachable via argv. I tested it at index 0, 1, 2, the last index, every index of an 8-char scheme, as a length-1 scheme, and inside the exhaustive 2-byte scan: always INVALID. Only 0x00 is genuinely unreachable, and it remains UNKNOWN.

(3) An unsupported "exhaustively verified" claim: '#' (0x23) and '?' (0x3F) cannot ever reach scheme(). parse() strips fragment then query from the whole URL before splitting on the first "://", so 'http#s://host' => 1|0|0|0|1|[http] — scheme is "" and LINE2=0 for the trivial empty-string reason, with LINE3=0/LINE5=1 violating the engineer's own hygiene filter. Those two bytes must be reclassified UNOBSERVABLE. Similarly, "no case folding" is unfalsifiable through this driver and should be stated as such rather than as a verified property.

Other things I tried that did NOT break it: percent-decoding in parse ('ht%74p://host' => 0, '%68ttp://host' => 0, so no decode); scheme truncation via embedded ':' and '/' ('a:b', 'a/b', 'a:', 'a:/', '::', 'a//', '//', ':a', '/a' — all 0, and 'a://b://c' => LINE2=1 confirming split on the FIRST "://"); locale switching including Latin-1 and Turkish; length interactions up to 65536; and any dependence of LINE 2 on host/port/path/query/fragment.

Relevant files I created (all throwaway probe scripts, absolute paths): /tmp/h.sh, /tmp/rand2.pl, /tmp/pos.pl, /tmp/pur.pl, /tmp/ex2.pl, /tmp/long.pl, /tmp/final.pl. Raw sweep data: /tmp/q0.txt (index 0), /tmp/q1.txt (index 1), /tmp/q3.txt (index 3), /tmp/len1.txt (length-1 schemes), /tmp/last2.txt (last index of length-2).
